programme: An epithelial identity-versus-plasticity switch: KLF4 and NKX2-1 are lineage-defining transcription factors that maintain differentiated epithelial identity and normally restrain EMT; PER2 directly represses the core EMT executors SNAI2 and TWIST1 (plus SERPINE1) as part of its target set, so loss of PER2 function de-represses them; FOXP4 acts as a direct YAP1/Hippo-pathway target that pushes cells toward an EMT-like stem state; HEYL, a Notch/HES-HEY-family effector, reinforces stromal and mesenchymal remodeling downstream of the same switch. Together these five factors form one identity-maintenance/plasticity-execution module rather than five unrelated hits.
role_in_a: In COVID-19, alveolar/airway epithelium undergoes an EMT-like transitional state during acute injury and post-acute fibrotic remodeling: NKX2-1 marks the alveolar epithelial transitional-cell state seen by BAL scRNA-seq, KLF4 transcriptional dynamics track post-COVID cardiovascular/fibrotic reprogramming, PER2-linked circadian disruption accompanies long-COVID fatigue, FOXP4 variants are genetically associated with long-COVID susceptibility, and HEYL promoter methylation tracks disease severity — consistent with this module being engaged during epithelial injury and its fibrotic aftermath.
role_in_b: In gastric cancer this is the canonical EMT/invasion-metastasis programme: KLF4 loss or functional inhibition permits EMT and invasion, PER2 knockdown removes repression of SNAI2/TWIST1 and drives a metabolically reprogrammed, immune-evasive mesenchymal state, FOXP4 is a direct YAP1 target promoting stemness and metastasis, HEYL appears in stromal/biomechanical gene signatures predicting recurrence, and NKX2-1/TTF1 status tracks a differentiation state whose disruption associates with more aggressive tumors.
shared_axis: Both settings recruit the same general-purpose epithelial plasticity toolkit — loss or downregulation of identity-maintaining factors (KLF4, NKX2-1) alongside activation of plasticity-driving effectors (PER2-target de-repression, FOXP4, HEYL) — because acute epithelial injury/repair in COVID-19 and tumor-associated invasion in gastric cancer both require a transient or sustained shift away from a stable differentiated epithelial state, even though the two diseases are not otherwise connected.
reasoning: No retrieved paper studies COVID-19 and gastric cancer jointly through these factors, so this is not an established shared axis; but each disease independently and specifically documents nearly every carrying factor (KLF4, NKX2-1, PER2, FOXP4, HEYL all have disease-specific PMIDs on both sides), and the module is nameable from the factors' own target genes (PER2→SNAI2/TWIST1 is a direct EMT-driver relationship, not an inference). Recurrence of 56-66/120 comparisons for each carrying factor is a real but partial signal, not near-unanimous, so the story should be read as a genuine subprogram rather than the dominant network signature.
support: 40819217 (KLF4 tracked in post-COVID cardiovascular transcriptional reprogramming); 41883394, 40504295, 40849587 (KLF4 mechanistically restrains EMT/invasion in gastric cancer); 37523502 (NKX2-1 marks alveolar epithelial transitional cells in COVID-19 BAL scRNA-seq); 36094595 (NKX2-1/TTF1 functional role in gastric transcriptome); 39896874 (PER2/circadian disruption in long-COVID fatigue); 41928364 (PER2 knockdown de-represses EMT/metabolic reprogramming and drives immunotherapy resistance in gastric cancer); 40724930, 40399555, 39298002 (FOXP4 genetic association with long-COVID); 39047223 (FOXP4 is a direct YAP1 target driving gastric cancer stemness/metastasis); 35655915 (HEYL promoter methylation predicts COVID-19 severity); 42445388, 41438119, 41608646, 34157940 (HEYL in stromal/biomechanical prognostic signatures in gastric cancer).
how_to_falsify: In matched airway/alveolar epithelial samples from acute and post-COVID patients and in paired gastric tumor/margin tissue, jointly profile the identity factors (KLF4, NKX2-1) against the EMT executors (SNAI2, TWIST1) and the two effectors (FOXP4, HEYL); the module predicts these should move as a coordinated unit (identity factors down, EMT/effector factors up) in both disease contexts. Alternatively, knock down PER2 in parallel in a SARS-CoV-2-infected airway organoid and a gastric cancer line: if SNAI2/TWIST1 derepression and an EMT-like phenotype do not both appear, the proposed shared mechanism is wrong.
caveats: The COVID-19 network here was built from blood, not lung tissue, so NKX2-1/KLF4 recurrence in a blood-derived network is a proxy signal (possibly circulating epithelial debris, cross-tissue eQTL, or leukocyte subsets) rather than direct lung-tissue evidence — the mechanistic lung papers cited (e.g., the BAL scRNA-seq study) are not from the same tissue as the network itself. Only 2 independent cohort pairs underlie the 120 patient-group comparisons, limiting true independence of the recurrence counts, and each carrying factor recurs in only about half of comparisons (56-66/120), so this is a partial subprogram, not a near-universal one. Six concordant factors (PEG3, MEIS3, HOXD3, POU3F1, CXXC1, HOXB3) had essentially no literature grounding in either disease per the reader's notes and were deliberately excluded rather than forced into the story. STAT4 has comparably good independent evidence in both diseases but operates through a distinct T-cell/cytokine-exhaustion axis, not through EMT, so it was left out of this specific programme. The tissue-generic exclusion list (BCL6, IRF5, IRF1, SPI1, FLI1, etc.) already removed likely confounding master immune regulators, so their absence here is expected, not a gap.
